. Every subsequent Wheel event is captur: . Every subsequent Wheel event is captured before nested panels and native browser scrolling, and is routed only to the locked level regardless of cursor position. Shift does not release the selection/override only when that exact selected level has a real horizontal scroll axis; Shift + Wheel then scrolls that same level horizontally. On a level without horizontal scrolling, Shift releases the selection/override like any other non-Ctrl/Command key. Any other key (including Tab, Escape, Enter, arrows or text input) and any pointer press (mouse, touch or pen; any mouse button) releases it without consuming the original input. Reaching an edge, becoming empty, or being temporarily rerendered never silently transfers scrolling to another level. Only layers with a genuinely visible, unobscured area participate: elements outside the viewport or fully covered by a higher stacking layer (for example underneath the sticky header, a dialog or an overlay) are excluded. Partially covered layers remain selectable through their still-visible area.

and replaces that exact entry, even when: and replaces that exact entry, even when the placed Composite still carries an older or missing saved identity. If name and fingerprint match, neither action is rendered. Renaming a placed Composite to a previously unused name therefore never overwrites its former saved entry; the new name is saved as a new entry. Ambiguous duplicate normalized names are blocked instead of updating an arbitrary entry or creating another duplicate. Legacy Composite JSON without a fingerprint is offered once by exact normalized name and receives its generated fingerprint when the update is accepted. Import scope follows the matching name across both locations: a Graph-only match updates only the placed graph and creates no Saved entry; a Saved-only match updates only the library; a match in both locations updates both; only a name found nowhere is imported as new. Existing duplicate Saved entries with that exact normalized name are consolidated into one retained identity during the confirmed update. A stale or orphaned Saved-Composite identity on a placed instance never blocks the name match. If any matching Composite is open, graph replacement is blocked for the complete target set; use the Breadcrumb to open its immediate parent graph before replacing from the Node Library. Every graph replacement preserves position and every external wire route whose published endpoint still exists under the resulting contract. Updating placed graphs is intentionally available only from the matching Saved Composite's arrow action in the Node Library. An upward arrow writes the currently open Composite to the Library; a downward arrow applies the Library version to placed graph instances. If the editor state changes before the click is committed, the action refreshes and aborts instead of silently reversing direction. The action is not rendered at all while every matching placed graph has the same content fingerprint; it appears only when at least one matching graph actually differs. Removed ports are reverse-mapped before confirmation; an ambiguous mapping aborts the complete replacement instead of guessing a new endpoint. Structurally invalid outward chains and their affected wires are removed as part of the confirmed change. Every Properties action button is re-evaluated immediately after its synchronous or asynchronous action completes. to reuse the complete internal graph. Sa: to reuse the complete internal graph. Saved Composites are also visible while an API Composite's internal graph is open, so another Saved Composite can be clicked or dragged from the Node Library into it as a complete nested Composite. Its internal nodes, boundaries, wire and branch routes, deeper nested Composites and owned Custom C# graphs stay hierarchical and are expanded recursively for generated code. The currently open Composite remains visible in the Library, but its insertion surface is grey and cannot be dragged into itself; its circular Update action remains available only after a real content change and then writes the open graph back to that Saved Composite. Direct and indirect recursive Library dependencies are rejected. Other Saved Composites can be inserted from the Node Library, unpacked, deleted, exported and imported as JSON, and are checked individually against the active verified catalog. Saving and importing preserve nested ownership, the outer Composite's switched port side and every internal node's port side. A Saved Composite's circular Update action also finds and replaces differing nested instances. Replacing with an older Saved Composite never silently deletes members that exist only in the placed instance: those nodes and complete nested Composites are moved back to their immediate parent graph, while compatible connection IDs, ports, wire points, branch routes and parent boundaries are rewritten through the previous boundary map. Boundary chains through parent and grandparent Composites are removed recursively when their source port is gone or becomes internally connected. Any affected outer wires and branch descendants are removed with that chain; a removed port is never recreated merely to preserve an old outer connection. Stable element identities make the comparison exact for new instances; legacy instances are accepted only after a deterministic structural match. If any connected element cannot be reconstructed unambiguously or the expanded result is invalid, the entire replacement is rejected and the original project remains unchanged. Every Saved Composite carries a content fingerprint derived from its normalized name, port order and side, complete node content and layout, connections, wire routes, branch routes and owned Custom C# graphs. Node Actions compares the Composite's current normalized name with the Saved Composite library: if no saved name matches,
